question: Find the least number of square tiles required to completely cover a floor of dimensions 12.15 m by 11.34 m.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the floor dimensions to cm: 1215 cm and 1134 cm.

Side of the largest square tile = HCF(1215, 1134) = 81 cm.

Total tiles = (1215 × 1134) ÷ (81 × 81).

Total tiles = 15 × 14 = 210.

**∴ The correct answer is 210.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the floor = 12.15 m = 1215 cm

Breadth of the floor = 11.34 m = 1134 cm

 
 Length = 12.15 m (1215 cm)

 Total Tiles = Area of Floor ÷ Area of 1 Tile

**Formula Used:**

Number of tiles = Total Area of Floor ÷ Area of one Tile

Maximum side of tile = HCF(Length, Breadth)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Side of the square tile = HCF of 1215 and 1134

⇒ Prime factorization of 1215 = 3⁵ × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 1134 = 2 × 3⁴ × 7

⇒ HCF(1215, 1134) = 3⁴ = 81 cm

⇒ Area of the floor = 1215 × 1134 cm²

⇒ Area of one square tile = 81 × 81 cm²

⇒ Total tiles required = (1215 × 1134) ÷ (81 × 81)

⇒ Total tiles required = (1215 ÷ 81) × (1134 ÷ 81)

⇒ Total tiles required = 15 × 14 = 210

**∴ The correct answer is 210.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Application of HCF in Mensuration

When completely covering a rectangular surface with maximum-sized square pieces without any cuts, the side length of the square piece must be the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the dimensions of the surface.

Prime Factorization for HCF

To find the HCF of two numbers, factorize them into prime numbers and multiply the lowest powers of all common prime factors present in both numbers.
